title: Foods to Skip Before Baby's First Birthday
hook: A few foods are genuinely risky for babies under one — honey can cause botulism, cow's milk shouldn't be the main drink yet, and round, hard foods are choking hazards.
key_points: No honey before 12 months — it can cause infant botulism, a serious illness.
Don't give cow's milk as your baby's main drink before 12 months; breast milk or formula stays the main drink.
Avoid choking hazards: whole grapes, nuts and seeds, popcorn, hard raw fruit or veg, and big chunks — cut food small and soft.
Limit added sugar and salt, and skip fruit juice for babies under one.
content_html: Once your baby starts solids, most family foods are fair game — but a short list is genuinely worth avoiding in the first year. The CDC flags honey first: don't give it before 12 months, because it can cause infant botulism, a serious form of food poisoning. Cow's milk is the other big one — it shouldn't be your baby's main drink before their first birthday, so breast milk or formula stays the main drink while solids fill in around it.
extra_html: Choking is the day-to-day risk to plan for. The CDC lists hazards like whole or uncut grapes and tomatoes, nuts and seeds, popcorn, spoonfuls of nut butter, and hard raw fruit or vegetables — so cut food small, soft, and easy to gum. It also recommends limiting added sugars and salt and skipping fruit juice entirely for babies under one. This is general guidance; your pediatrician can help with introducing foods, allergens, and your baby's specific needs.

related.title: Starting Solid Foods
related.hook: Most babies are ready for their first solid foods at around six months — alongside continued breast milk or formula, not instead of it.

related.title: Picky Eating Is Normal
related.hook: Picky eating is a normal toddler stage, not a battle to win. The reliable approach: you decide what and when to offer, your child decides whether and how much to eat.

flashcards.prompt: Why is honey off-limits before 12 months?

choices.text: It can cause infant botulism, a serious illness
It's too sweet for a baby's taste buds

flashcards.explanation_html: The CDC advises no honey before 12 months because it can cause botulism, a severe form of food poisoning in infants.

flashcards.prompt: Which of these is a choking hazard to avoid giving as-is to a baby?
flashcards.explanation_html: Round, hard, or chunky foods like whole grapes, nuts, and popcorn are choking hazards. Cut foods small and soft instead.

flashcards.prompt: Should cow's milk be a baby's main drink before their first birthday?
flashcards.back_html: No. Breast milk or formula stays the main drink in the first year. The CDC advises against cow's milk as the main drink before 12 months.
